deep.reconstruction:
The page opens a short axiomatic treatment of 'equisingularity'. Grothendieck intends it to work in several 'contexts': topological spaces, algebraic or analytic spaces, and piecewise-linear spaces. 'Espace' (and a second, hard-to-read word, most likely 'morphisme' or 'application') denote the objects and morphisms of whichever context is chosen.

(1) Basic definition. Let X be a space and Y a locally closed subspace. X is equisingular along Y if every y in Y has an open neighbourhood X' in X and a pointed space (Z,a) with an isomorphism of pairs (X', Y' = X'∩Y) ≅ (Y'×Z, Y'×{a}), compatible with the identity of Y'. In modern terms, the pair (X,Y) is locally trivial along Y with 'normal slice' (Z,a). This is the local topological triviality of a stratum, as in Thom–Mather theory and in Siebenmann's locally cone-like stratified sets. Z is not required to be a cone.

(2) Generalisation to diagrams. Let 𝒳 = (X_i), i in I, be a diagram of spaces indexed by a small category I; only posets are envisaged. Fix i0 in I and Y ⊂ X_{i0} locally closed. Let J be the full subdiagram of the j admitting an arrow to i0 (or equal to i0). 𝒳 is equisingular along Y if, for each y in Y, there are:
- a neighbourhood X'_{i0} of y in X_{i0},
- a diagram (Z_j), j in J, with a base point a in Z_{i0},
- a morphism of diagrams (Z_j × Y') → (X_j), with Y' = Y∩X'_{i0},
such that each Z_j×Y' → X_j is an open embedding and Y' ↪ X'_{i0} is identified with {a}×Y' ↪ Z_{i0}×Y'. This is simultaneous local triviality of a whole diagram of spaces along a subspace: a 'stratified local product structure' for diagrams.

Purpose (next page): apply this to a closed filtration X_0 ⊂ X_1 ⊂ … ⊂ X along the strata V_i = X_i − X_{i−1}. This defines equisingular filtrations, whose 'leaves' (connected components of the V_i) satisfy the frontier condition: the closure of a leaf is a union of leaves. This is part of Grothendieck's 'tame topology' programme on stratified structures, later sketched in the Esquisse d'un programme.
errors: Direction of arrows in J looks wrong for the intended application. With J = {j : j→i0}, i.e. the X_j mapping into X_{i0}, take a filtration and Y = V_i = X_i − X_{i−1} with i0 = i. The X_j for j<i are closed in X_i and disjoint from V_i. Locally near Y they are therefore empty, and the condition says nothing about how the larger X_j (j>i) sit around V_i. To recover local triviality of the filtration along V_i one needs J = {j : i0→j} (the spaces containing X_{i0}), with the neighbourhood taken in those larger spaces. Alternatively Grothendieck intends some reversed convention not stated on the page.

The open embeddings Z_j×Y' → X_j are not required to have image equal to the restriction of the chosen neighbourhood, e.g. X_j ∩ (preimage of X'_{i0}). Without this, the maps are local trivialisations only of some open pieces, not of a neighbourhood of Y in each X_j. This is a gap in the formulation.
Notation is inconsistent: Z'_{i0} and Z'_j appear where Z_{i0} and Z_j are meant, and the order of factors switches between Y'×Z and Z×Y'. These are harmless slips.

ideas.what: Equisingularity of X along locally closed Y as local product structure of the pair (X,Y) ≅ (Y'×Z, Y'×{a})
ideas.modern_name: Topological local triviality along a stratum / locally trivial (Thom–Mather, Siebenmann locally cone-like) stratifications
ideas.usually_credited_to: Whitney, Thom (1960s), Mather (1970), Siebenmann (1972); equisingularity programme of Zariski
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme (1984), §5 on tame topology and stratified structures, discusses equisingularity informally; no such formal definition there to my knowledge

ideas.what: Context-independent formulation: same definition meant for topological, algebraic, analytic and PL spaces
ideas.usually_credited_to: van den Dries and others (o-minimality, 1980s–90s), motivated partly by Grothendieck's Esquisse

ideas.what: Equisingularity of a poset-indexed diagram of spaces along a subspace of one vertex: simultaneous local trivialisation of the diagram by a diagram of normal slices (Z_j) times Y'
ideas.modern_name: Local triviality of stratified spaces/maps in families; cf. Thom's isotopy lemmas, conically stratified spaces (Lurie, Higher Algebra A.5), local triviality of filtered spaces
ideas.usually_credited_to: Thom–Mather (isotopy lemmas), Quinn and Hughes (filtered/homotopically stratified spaces), Lurie (exit-path ∞-categories)

missed.claim: A general, context-free notion of equisingularity for diagrams of spaces indexed by a poset, rather than only for a single stratified space. This is a natural device for treating stratifications, stratified maps and their compatibility uniformly. The draft here has an apparent direction error and was never published.
missed.quote: Plus généralement, soit 𝒳=(X_i)_{i∈I} un diagramme d'espaces ... On dit que 𝒳 est équisingulier le long de Y si ...
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It anticipates treating stratified objects as diagrams indexed by the stratification poset, as in exit-path and conically stratified approaches. However, the content is close to standard local triviality, so its novelty is modest.

deep.surprise_reason: These are careful foundational definitions of topological local triviality, in line with Thom–Mather and Siebenmann and with Grothendieck's tame-topology programme. The diagram generalisation and the multi-context framing are mildly interesting, but not substantively new.
transcription_corrections: 'Le mot "espace" et "stratifié"' – the second quoted word is unclear in the image. Given 'désignent des objets et morphismes', it is most likely 'morphisme' or 'application', not 'stratifié'.
'avec $Z'_{i_0}$ muni d'un point' should read 'avec $Z_{i_0}$ muni d'un point $a\in Z_{i_0}$'.
'ou bien j=i_0 ou bien' is an interlinear insertion qualifying 'les j∈I pour lesquels ∃ flèche j→i_0'. It belongs before '∃ flèche', and is followed by '; ∀y∈Y on peut trouver'.
'$Z'_j\times Y'\to X_j$' should be '$Z_j\times Y'\to X_j$'.
'Équisingularité' heading and '(Z,a)' as 'espace pointé' are correct.
